221 |         # Pad tokens
222 |         num_padding_tokens = self.max_seq_len - len(pack["tokens"])
223 |         padded_tokens = F.pad(

234 |         )
235 | 
236 |         # Add padding tokens as a last seq len to ensure sum is max_seq_len
237 |         padded_seq_lens = (
238 |             torch.cat([pack["seq_lens"], torch.tensor([num_padding_tokens])])
239 |             if num_padding_tokens > 0
240 |             else pack["seq_lens"]
241 |         )

105 |         until max_packs or end of dataset."""

107 |         current_pack = {
108 |             "tokens": [],
109 |             "labels": [],
110 |             "input_pos": [],
111 |             "seq_lens": [],
112 |         }
113 | 
114 |         # Only show progress bar on rank 0
115 |         rank = (
116 |             torch.distributed.get_rank()
117 |             if torch.distributed.is_available() and torch.distributed.is_initialized()
118 |             else 0
119 |         )
120 |         if rank == 0:
121 |             pbar = tqdm(total=len(self.ds), desc="Packing dataset", dynamic_ncols=True)
122 | 
123 |         for sample in self.ds:
124 |             tokens, labels = sample["tokens"], sample["labels"]
125 | 
126 |             # If the dataset outputs samples that are larger than the specified
127 |             # max_seq_len and we're unable to split it, user needs to modify
128 |             # one of the two parameters
129 |             seq_len = len(tokens)

131 |                 raise ValueError(

135 | 
136 |             # Update the current pack

138 |             current_pack["labels"] += labels
139 |             current_pack["input_pos"] += list(range(seq_len))
140 |             current_pack["seq_lens"] += [seq_len]
141 | 
142 |             # If the current pack is over the max_seq_len, add it to self.packs and
143 |             # retain any truncated or bumped samples for next pack
144 |             if len(current_pack["tokens"]) > self.max_seq_len:

146 | 
147 |             if rank == 0:

149 | 
150 |             # Keep track of previous sample boundary
151 |             self.previous_sample_boundary = len(current_pack["tokens"])
152 | 
153 |             # If max packs is set, stop packing when we reach that number
154 |             if self.max_packs is not None and len(self.packs) == self.max_packs:

15 | def left_pad_sequence(
16 |     sequences: List[torch.Tensor],
17 |     batch_first: bool = False,
18 |     padding_value: float = 0,
19 | ) -> torch.Tensor:
20 |     """
21 |     This function is identical to :func:`torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_sequence`, but
22 |     instead pads a list of variable length Tensors from the left to the length
23 |     of the longest sequence.
24 | 
25 |     Note:
26 |         This function returns a Tensor of size ``T x B x *`` or ``B x T x *``
27 |         where `T` is the length of the longest sequence. This function assumes
28 |         trailing dimensions and type of all the Tensors in sequences are same.
29 | 
30 |     Args:
31 |         sequences (List[torch.Tensor]): list of variable length sequences.
32 |         batch_first (bool): if ``True``, the output will be in ``B x T x *``
33 |             format, ``T x B x *`` otherwise. Default False.
34 |         padding_value (float): value for padded elements. Default: 0.
35 | 
36 |     Returns:
37 |         Tensor of size ``T x B x *`` if :attr:`batch_first` is ``False``.
38 |         Tensor of size ``B x T x *`` otherwise
39 | 
40 |     Example:
41 |         >>> a = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3])
42 |         >>> b = torch.tensor([4, 5, 6, 7])
43 |         >>> c = torch.tensor([8, 9, 10, 11, 12])
44 |         >>> left_pad_sequence([a, b, c], batch_first=True, padding_value=0)
45 |         tensor([[ 0,  0,  1,  2,  3],
46 |                 [ 0,  4,  5,  6,  7],
47 |                 [ 8,  9, 10, 11, 12]])
48 |     """
49 |     return pad_sequence(
50 |         map(lambda x: torch.flip(x, dims=[0]), sequences),
51 |         batch_first=batch_first,
52 |         padding_value=padding_value,
53 |     ).flip(dims=[int(batch_first)])

114 | def packed_block_causal_mask(
115 |     seq_lens: List[torch.Tensor],
116 | ) -> _MaskType:
117 |     """
118 |     Create a block causal document mask for a batch of packed sequences. If on
119 |     torch version >= 2.5.0, this is done by creating a mask_mod function with the
120 |     block causal logic and passing this into :func:`torch.nn.attention.flex_attention.create_block_mask`.
121 |     The resultant BlockMask is a compressed representation of the full block causal
122 |     mask. If on an older version, a standard 2D block causal mask is created and returned.
123 | 
124 |     Args:
125 |         seq_lens (List[torch.Tensor]): Sequence lengths of samples in each pack in the batch,
126 |             shape (batch_size, n), where n is the max number of sequences in a pack and can vary
127 |             across packs.
128 | 
129 |     Returns:
130 |         _MaskType: BlockMask or Tensor if torch version < 2.5.0.
131 |     """
132 |     if _SUPPORTS_FLEX_ATTENTION:
133 |         document_ids = _get_document_ids_from_seq_lens(seq_lens)
134 |         batch_size, max_seq_len = document_ids.shape
135 |         document_ids = document_ids.to("cuda")
136 | 
137 |         # Instead of passing a tensor mask, flex attention requires a mask_mod function
138 |         # that determines which elements of QK^T should be included in the attention
139 |         # computation prior to the softmax. For sample packing, we need both the
140 |         # logic for both causal mask and document mask. See PyTorch's official
141 |         # blog post for more details: https://pytorch.org/blog/flexattention/#mask-mods
142 |         def mask_mod(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
143 |             """
144 |             Defines the logic of a block causal mask by combining both a standard causal mask
145 |             and a block diagonal document mask.
146 | 
147 |             See :func:`~torchtune.modules.attention_utils.create_block_causal_mask`
148 |             for an illustration.
149 |             """
150 |             causal_mask = q_idx >= kv_idx
151 |             document_mask = document_ids[b, q_idx] == document_ids[b, kv_idx]
152 |             return causal_mask & document_mask
153 | 
154 |         return create_block_causal_mask_flex(
155 |             mask_mod,
156 |             batch_size,
157 |             None,
158 |             max_seq_len,
159 |             max_seq_len,
160 |             device="cuda",
161 |         )
162 |     else:
163 |         return create_block_causal_mask(seq_lens=seq_lens)

45 | def _get_document_ids_from_seq_lens(
46 |     seq_lens: List[torch.Tensor],
47 | ) -> torch.Tensor:
48 |     """
49 |     Convert a batch tensor of seq lens into integer IDs denoting sample ownership.
50 |     For example, seq_lens = [2, 3, 1] would return [0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2].
51 | 
52 |     Args:
53 |         seq_lens (List[torch.Tensor]): Sequence lengths of samples in each pack in the batch,
54 |             shape (batch_size, n), where n is the max number of sequences in a pack and can vary
55 |             across packs.
56 | 
57 |     Returns:
58 |         Tensor: Document IDs of shape (batch_size, max_seq_len).
59 |     """
60 |     batch_size = len(seq_lens)
61 |     batch_document_ids = []
62 |     for sample_idx in range(batch_size):
63 |         # We assume seq lens sum to max seq lens, so document_ids should be of
64 |         # shape (max_seq_len, )
65 |         document_ids = torch.cat(
66 |             [
67 |                 torch.full((seq_len,), i, dtype=torch.long, device=seq_len.device)
68 |                 for i, seq_len in enumerate(seq_lens[sample_idx])
69 |             ]
70 |         )
71 |         batch_document_ids.append(document_ids)
72 |     batch_document_ids = torch.stack(batch_document_ids)
73 |     return batch_document_ids
